product: alt-context WP plugin admin SPA — describe run GPU tier + lifecycle state
goals: UXREC-1 target contract (proposed; not current source): unknown or stale GPU observation, an accepted warming or running run, and a genuine run failure are separate states. GPU status carries no configuration or capability field, so no surface infers configuration or CPU capability from unknown telemetry ([HAI-05] Imperceptible AI is not ethical, Human-Centered AI). Code references are anchors, not implementation claims.

An accepted run exposes its observed startup state, its actual startup bound, Cancel and return-to-run ([INT-10] Status–predict–stop, Human-Centered AI); historical cold-start measurements are not a current ETA.

Three outcomes stay distinct: GPU success (items report the final GPU tier); CPU completion after a warm-up timeout, only when a usable CPU adapter is configured (the run reports fallback reason gpu_warmup_timeout and items report the provisional CPU tier); typed warm-up failure with no CPU (FAILED terminal gpu_warmup_timeout, Retry only when retryable, no drafts). There is no automatic CPU-to-GPU draft upgrade, and draft review exists only when the run reports completed items.

Visible copy fix: the warming and degraded toasts (GPU_STATE_VOCABULARY warmingToast and degradedToast, emitted by useGpuStateToasts) name only the observed GPU state and never claim CPU drafts without returned evidence. Canonical state labels, dormant unavailable-toast suppression, real results and their review actions, and genuine failure, cancel and retry stay. Editing the unused gpuStateNotice / notReportedNotice helper is cleanup, not the visible fix.

endpoint_unconfigured copy belongs only where an actual unavailable envelope with that reason is received: the shared unavailable-reason copy table and its existing consumers (Settings GPU control and Retention, mapped elsewhere). The bulk describe-run submit returns no such envelope, and unknown or stale status telemetry never shows configuration copy; a status-contract configuration field is a separate backend task.

Before Describe, disclose possible GPU warm-up and infrastructure charges separately from credits, with a Settings link (INT-07, NAV-11). Read failures retain saved rows and apply recovery, show a stale notice, and offer a read-only Retry (INT-10).

screens.title: Workbench › Media selection
screens.purpose: Select media and describe. UXREC-1 proposed quiet unknown copy: GPU tier not reported; description readiness is unconfirmed; no idle failure toast. Existing tenant-scoped operation storage resumes an accepted run_id on remount without resubmission; this is source behavior, runtime acceptance pending.

zones.label: Describe selected; selection and service readiness are separate. Unknown GPU copy makes no CPU or configuration claim and does not disable an otherwise legal submission; no new readiness API.

Accepted run only: starting, warming or running with observed state, actual startup bound, Cancel and return-to-run. Terminal captions stay distinct: GPU success; CPU completion after warm-up timeout (reported fallback reason, provisional CPU items); typed warm-up failure with no drafts and Retry only when retryable. Cancelled and other failures keep their existing outcomes.

State vocabulary: hidden-no-run = empty; unknown = default. GPU observation is not description readiness: unknown stays quiet with neutral copy; starting, warming, ready and degraded never certify results or CPU capability; canonical state labels are unchanged.

Review & apply drafts link — only for a terminal run that reports completed items, linking #/workbench?hasDraft=1&run=<id>; absent after a failure that returned no drafts; shows the reported item tier and never promises an upgrade.
Recovery contract: read-only status retry does not restart inference; remount resumes stored tenant run_id; cancellation acknowledgement ends pending state; rejected persistence remains visible.

screens.title: Media library description review › Review & apply
screens.purpose: Review, edit and explicitly approve each image draft beside saved alt text. The run query parameter previews that run; the visible version chooser selects previous descriptions. Loading = loading; no drafts = empty; unavailable history = error or degraded. No selection saves automatically. Serves job `gpu-tier-awareness`.

zones.label: Per-image draft and saved-alt distinction, with version run/time provenance. Shows the reported item tier (final GPU or provisional CPU) and naming provenance from the existing result API; never infers a tier from run failure or GPU state.

No upgrade notice: provisional CPU drafts stay as returned; there is no automatic CPU-to-GPU upgrade, and any GPU result comes only from a later, explicitly started run. GPU readiness never promises final descriptions.

screens.title: Dashboard › Describe with AI
screens.purpose: Single-image describe; shows adapter/model provenance. Run phases: result = default; submitting = loading. Serves job `single-describe`.

zones.label: Provenance (Adapter / Model / Source / Latency) — State vocabulary: gpu and seeded = default; cpu (provisional tier) = degraded.
Inline error (role=alert) — State vocabulary: hidden = empty; generic = error; gpu-unreachable = offline.

screens.title: Toast — GPU tier transition
screens.purpose: Preserve source suppression of dormant GPU_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE when runId is null; genuine in-run failures and actual completion remain meaningful feedback. UXREC-1 visible fix: the warming and degraded toasts name only the observed GPU state and never claim CPU drafts; no per-poll notices.

zones.label: Toast body — info and success = default; error = error. Done reports the actual completed count and offers Review drafts only when that count is above zero; failure names its typed cause, with Retry only when retryable.

actions.verb: Review returned drafts (only when the run reports completed items)

flows.label: GPU success: cold GPU becomes ready within the startup bound

steps.branch_label: select → readiness/cost preview; unknown GPU observation is not a CPU or configuration claim
accepted run → observed starting/warming with its actual startup bound and Cancel; no fixed ETA
GPU ready within the bound → describing on GPU → terminal; items report the final GPU tier
only if the operator left: Done reports the completed count; Review drafts only when that count is above zero
Review each returned draft, preview an earlier version, edit or explicitly accept; saved alt text changes only on approval

flows.label: Conditional CPU completion: warm-up times out and a usable CPU adapter is configured

steps.branch_label: accepted run warming → the actual startup bound expires
only with a usable configured CPU adapter: the run continues on CPU, reports fallback reason gpu_warmup_timeout, and items report the provisional CPU tier
only if the operator left: Done reports the completed count without a GPU-result claim; Review drafts only when that count is above zero
review provisional CPU drafts as returned; no automatic GPU upgrade; acceptance stays explicit

flows.label: Typed failure without CPU: warm-up times out and no usable CPU adapter exists

steps.branch_label: accepted run warming → the actual startup bound expires with no usable CPU adapter
run FAILED with typed warm-up timeout: no CPU drafts are created or promised, saved alt text is unchanged, Retry only when retryable
only if the operator left: the failure toast names the warm-up timeout, with Retry only when retryable; no draft review

flows.label: Dashboard single describe on GPU tier

steps.branch_label: submit → result; z-provenance shows Adapter=gpu_qwen30b, Model
GPU stopped → z-inline-error gpu-unreachable names the state + what to do

flows.label: Source persistence regression: navigation and reload

steps.branch_label: accepted run_id persisted under tenant; leave or reload while warming
remount resumes status reads for same run_id without POST duplicate; unavailable observation stays unknown; Cancel remains available
only when the resumed run reports completed items: those returned drafts become reviewable; acceptance is explicit, never automatic

open_questions: Should the WP operator ever get an explicit 'Start GPU' / 'Stop GPU' control (HAI-04 activate–operate–override), or is warm-on-enqueue + idle reap the only lifecycle (DEMO-UX-1-GPU-01 proposes enqueue-triggered start)? Current recommendation: no manual control in the plugin; CTA discloses the cost and lifecycle is implicit.
gpu_state source of truth: lifecycle reaper writes /run/acx/gpu-state.json vs API probes ACX_GPU_ENDPOINT_URL/health. One writer only (DATA-14).
Toast when the operator IS on the progress screen: suppress (double announcement with the polite live region, A11Y-21) — confirm with a screen-reader pass.

UXREC-1: no runtime window granted. Validate starting/results and remount on exact deployment separately; API health and recognition policy do not establish description readiness. No new GPU controls in this slice.
not_doing: No confirm tab / modal before bulk describe (workbench not-doing inherited); cost disclosure lives in the CTA label + CTA hint.
No per-poll toasts; no toast for provisional→final per item.
No GPU cost meter in the plugin (billing is operator-side, OCI).
No automatic CPU-to-GPU draft upgrade, and no CPU-continuation promise from unknown, stale or degraded GPU state.

No backend status schema or configuration/capability field, GPU automation, authorization bypass, billing or credential change; operator-tenant GPU authorization and id path-segment encoding stay unchanged.
